### Key Risks

- **Liver damage (acetaminophen):** Alcohol changes how the liver processes acetaminophen, which can increase toxic byproducts and harm the liver. Risk is highest with heavy or regular drinking (often flagged on labels as 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day), binge drinking, or taking high doses of acetaminophen.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF18933urtJJWCrWH21MRTvYd80YMQsQuphomsQ-k6O8G5ySscRW8ALaFwhfCR0w1VFda-EGRsBdBMDphjR2OBxHrzJMSQi7M7i_vnHDzsqqmQqZaI7Gs0iZdDKBlBd4y2oXfqVpqVkrKJ8U90bWEXhtNAcT3RXGswiUKwt8yTa6fn2L4gJZHOtmnCOg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXXc9Hgy72H2RDUUYAmJrP4ZkFF9pEr6c_dwZueED3tcrIsdbZ8jNdLWLWi9sxdQZnkxEN66xClekcJkkQ6r9poP72eg_Vyy_i3VGEHJnSshVl5DWJvarBUaCZ4GY1k5IEwbC9ZSkIu8RNzpnCmcQeITQdvOX1sfDPOLv8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXW7Fa0lRB3W3uSQeuFSvcCxZMS1pyX0lhmN7XUAHfD_fiGZe8Nrvv1uCFtNrDtzxbbgvZh_LUkjFr7sxBAm0sQFyKwrRAQOVYxVfe_bcTnJ6czqBg4KNBRsfruinic2FVgj_PcCWO3DLfW3erOKpEyrUNyQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF135G475MpHdo-qm4BIyw0CnFWLSvNCejH8Pyf0PSCjqcbHjThYSyL_XYeD2oO5WVi6NuVSwk_UGqkq3WhZ6_OAGB8vySESYyetzMCcPb6YtVjzoLtgURuWEc9j_6pDPindRVbZPrModEY6Fa0mS9etenmPW-llmvz3lYdORPlsC71qJ1vscMzIRu9g)

items.text: Liver damage (acetaminophen): Alcohol changes how the liver processes acetaminophen, which can increase toxic byproducts and harm the liver. Risk is highest with heavy or regular drinking (often flagged on labels as 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day), binge drinking, or taking high doses of acetaminophen. Stomach bleeding (aspirin): Both alcohol and aspirin can irritate the stomach lining. Mixing them raises the chance of gastritis, ulcers, or stomach bleeding—especially if you drink frequently, are 60 or older, or take blood thinners or other NSAIDs. Stomach upset and heart effects: Combining alcohol and caffeine can worsen stomach irritation, nausea, or jitteriness, and pain relievers mixed with alcohol may contribute to a rapid heartbeat.
